key_claims: Higher cardiovascular risk factor burden is linearly associated with lower cerebral arterial elasticity.
The relationship between age and cerebral arterial elasticity is partially mediated by pulse pressure.
Cerebral arterial elasticity declined significantly over 1.5 years.
The decline in cerebral arterial elasticity did not vary with baseline level of any of the four cardiovascular risk factors.
PReFx shows promise as a putative biomarker for monitoring cerebrovascular ageing in healthy older adults.
limitations: The study cohort is highly active and cognitively healthy, limiting generalizability.
The study does not establish causality.
The study does not report effect sizes or confidence intervals.
The study does not compare PReFx to other biomarkers.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that cardiovascular risk factors cause reduced cerebral arterial elasticity.
The study shows that PReFx is a validated clinical biomarker.
The study provides specific numerical values for the decline in PReFx.
The study includes participants outside the 60-70 age range.
The study demonstrates that reducing cardiovascular risk factors improves cerebral arterial elasticity.
